operations.name: Frank Westerlund

expected.charges: Federal prosecution under the Espionage Act of 1917 and/or the Sedition Act of 1918 (mass IWW trial in Chicago).
expected.sentence:
Five years in prison (Espionage/Sedition Act conviction).

ADMITTED TO BAIL, APRIL 2, 1919. The Federal Circuit Court of Appeals ordered thirty-eight of the men convicted in the Chicago mass trial released on bail pending its review of the case; the bonds ran from $5,000 to $10,000, with Haywood alone required to provide $15,000. Fifty-five others convicted in the same case did not seek bail. The order is not the release: each man left Leavenworth when his bond was actually furnished, which for those whose dates are recorded here fell between April 28 and September 28, 1919. Reported in the New York Times and across the wire services, April 3, 1919.

updates.convicted: Seditious conspiracy; U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois

operations.source: Primary Senate Document159,Government Prosecutions Under the Espionage Act (1922): https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/SERIALSET-07987_00_00-063-0159-0000/pdf/SERIALSET-07987_00_00-063-0159-0000.pdf . operations.name: Homer C. Spence

expected.sentence:
Tenant farmer and Working Class Union organizer tied to the Green Corn Rebellion of August 2–3, 1917, an armed antiwar uprising against WWI and the Selective Service Act. Already out on bail for obstructing the 1917 draft, he was tried for conspiracy and given ten years at Leavenworth — one of the heaviest sentences on a Green Corn organizer — before Harding pardoned him in 1921

Verdict as recorded: Convicted of conspiracy; sentenced to ten years; pardoned by President Warren G. Harding in 1921
